name: Cinzel (wght 500)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/cinzel/
why: The Trajan-descended baseline: carved-stone caps say 'dark fantasy' instantly, but it is the overused Dark Souls-era look and carries no personality of its own.

name: Cinzel Decorative (Bold)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/cinzeldecorative/
why: Swash P, L and A turn the Roman baseline into reliquary engraving, a title that looks cut into a casket lid, though the flourishes get busy at capsule size.

name: Marcellus
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/marcellus/
why: Flared, chisel-cut Roman capitals with a gentle lowercase: stone-inscription authority with less genre cliche than Trajan.

name: Forum
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/forum/
why: Wide, light Renaissance Roman capitals; a quiet museum-plaque voice that suits a game about letting go, but thin for a small capsule.

name: Cormorant SC (SemiBold)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/cormorantsc/
why: Razor-serifed Garamond small capitals read as an engraved bookplate, the most elegant Trajan alternative while staying sharp enough for a logo.

name: IM Fell English
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/imfellenglish/
why: Roughened, ink-bled edges echo the slightly worn gold lettering of the It Follows cover and read as a surviving printed page, not a game.

name: IM Fell Double Pica
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/imfelldoublepica/
why: The Fell Types' baroque Roman with worn ink edges: the same 'old printed book' feel as the It Follows cover, a little narrower and more textured.

name: EB Garamond (wght 500)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/ebgaramond/
why: Closest free match to the It Follows cover lettering (use medium weight): a sturdy, soft Garamond that reads as a bound book, not a game.

name: Cormorant Garamond (wght 500)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/cormorantgaramond/
why: A delicate, tall-ascendered Garamond that is elegant and bookish but too light to survive a Steam capsule without a heavier cut.

name: Sorts Mill Goudy
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/sortsmillgoudy/
why: Warm, wide Goudy forms with soft bracketed serifs, close to the cover's proportions but gentler and more hand-pressed than ominous.

name: Libre Caslon Display
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/librecaslondisplay/
why: Hairline-serifed Caslon display gives a rare-book title page that holds at large sizes but loses its hairlines on a small library logo.

name: UnifrakturMaguntia
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/unifrakturmaguntia/
why: True Fraktur with sweeping capitals recalls lettered speech scrolls in medieval art, but all-caps it turns illegible and heavy-metal while mixed-case 'Phylactery' works.

name: Pirata One
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/pirataone/
why: A condensed, angular blackletter-lite that is instantly legible but pushes a pirate/metal menace too loud for a quiet game about giving things up.

name: Grenze Gotisch (wght 600)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/grenzegotisch/
why: Squared, heavy Gothic cut like woodtype from a scroll caption, striking as a title though the long Y tail makes the all-caps line ragged.

name: Jacquard 24
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/jacquard24/
why: A pixel-built blackletter that bridges the game's current pixel UI font and the medieval phylactery-scroll idea.

name: Texturina (opsz 72, wght 600)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/texturina/
why: A calm textura-inspired Roman that reads more rustic chapbook than gothic scroll, human rather than metal.

name: Fruktur
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/fruktur/
why: Brushy, bouncing Fraktur-derived forms with plenty of character but a cartoonish tone for a game about sacrifice.

name: Uncial Antiqua
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/uncialantiqua/
why: Rounded uncial forms with tall P and L evoke Insular manuscripts and the egg's curves, an overtly monastic, rebirth-flavoured voice.

name: MedievalSharp
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/medievalsharp/
why: Angular pen-cut medieval caps with sharp joins and runic-adjacent flair, legible but slightly costume-fantasy.

name: Mystery Quest
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/mysteryquest/
why: Curled, swashing storybook caps with spirals inside the letters read as whimsical spooky and miss the solemn lich tone.

name: Almendra Display
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/almendradisplay/
why: Hairline calligraphic caps with long swash tails evoke a reliquary inscription or alchemical plate, but the hairline weight vanishes at capsule size.

name: Spirax
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/spirax/
why: Art-nouveau curls on the Y, L and E read like an apothecary or alchemist's label, giving the lich a decorative, bottled-power register.

name: Elsie Swash Caps (Black)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/elsieswashcaps/
why: A fat Didone with ball terminals and long swashes is theatrical Victorian poster style, more circus than tomb.

name: Vast Shadow
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/vastshadow/
why: A slab serif with a built-in inline drop-shadow gives a sign-painter's engraved look, more Western saloon than reliquary.

name: Tilt Prism
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/tiltprism/
why: Bevelled, inline capitals look like faceted glass, a direct nod to the prism, gem and lens powers, though the thin outline struggles at small sizes.

name: Bodoni Moda (opsz 96, wght 600)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/bodonimoda/
why: Ultra-high-contrast Didone with near-invisible hairlines is the fashion-cover register of the Kaen side, glamorous and brittle but fragile on a capsule.

name: Playfair Display (wght 700)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/playfairdisplay/
why: A sturdy bold transitional Didone with magazine-cover confidence, high-contrast without losing its hairlines at small sizes.

name: Fraunces (opsz 144, wght 600, WONK 1)
designer_or_foundry: Undercase Type, Phaedra Charles, Flavia Zimbardi
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/fraunces/
why: A soft, quirky 'old-style Didone' with ink-trap curves bridges book and fashion, warm in the cave light yet unmistakably contemporary.

name: Instrument Serif
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/instrumentserif/
why: A condensed editorial serif with tall stems feels like a quiet modern album sleeve and fits narrow hero-banner space.

name: Syne (wght 800)
designer_or_foundry: Bonjour Monde, Lucas Descroix, George Triantafyllakos
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/syne/
why: An extra-wide ExtraBold grotesque gives a gallery-poster voice that bluntly contradicts the cave and book mood.

name: Unbounded (wght 700)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/unbounded/
why: A rounded, ultra-wide heavy sans is gamey and contemporary and clashes with the gothic subject.

name: Big Shoulders Display (wght 800)
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/bigshouldersdisplay/
why: A tall condensed industrial grotesque fits banner shapes and Kaen-style poster impact but reads sports/industrial, not medieval.

name: Anton
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/anton/
why: A heavy condensed gothic sans with loud poster legibility at any size (Kaen jacket register) but zero medieval or reliquary cue.

name: Cardo
licence: OFL 1.1 (free, commercial use allowed); TTF + OFL.txt in ttf/cardo/
why: Wide, bookish Renaissance Roman with large x-height, the best free match to the cover's wide proportions after EB Garamond.

name: PP Editorial New
licence: commercial, licences from $40 per style (full-family and app/game-embedding terms per Pangram Pangram FAQ); specimen is the foundry's own 'MoMA Book Fair' in-use image
why: A light, sharp-serifed Roman set in flat red on cream mirrors the flat-colour-field editorial look of the Kaen jacket and would give PHYLACTERY a fashion-masthead voice.

name: GT Sectra
licence: commercial, per-style Desktop / Web / App licences (prices only in the shop; embedding/unlimited by enquiry, unlimited from $10,000 per style); specimen is the foundry's own development diagram
why: Letterforms derived from a broad-nib pen and then cut with a scalpel give blade-sharp calligraphic terminals, a ritual-knife precision that suits sacrifice and bone.

name: Canela Collection
licence: commercial, Canela family $325, Canela Text $350, full collection $800 (desktop, one-time; app and web licences priced on request)
why: A Caslon-derived serif with only vestigial flaring and a stone-carving lineage is the contemporary descendant of Trajan-style inscription without the dark-fantasy cliche.

name: Druk Collection
licence: commercial, Druk collection $600 (families $150-$200, desktop, one-time; app and web licences by enquiry)
why: Heavy compressed Druk is the poster voice of fashion and streetwear covers, the loudest possible Kaen-side wordmark and a hard counterweight to the gothic lettering.

name: Dark Souls (Remastered) logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Wide, distressed Roman capitals with a hairline cut through the middle; no authoritative font credit exists (some font-ID sites claim Adobe Garamond Bold, unverified), so treat as custom lettering; it defines the stone-carved, scratched dark-fantasy look to avoid copying.

name: Elden Ring logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Chisel-cut Roman capitals with long spurs, rendered as gold-cream cracked stone; custom lettering (no font credit found), and the closest game precedent for gold-on-black as a material.

name: Hollow Knight logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Condensed Roman capitals framed by a symmetrical bug-and-filigree ornament; appears custom (community guesses of Trajan Pro and Perpetua are unsourced), a title card that reads like a bookplate.

name: Blasphemous logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Lowercase blackletter-derived lettering in gold-foil texture; appears custom (no font credit found) and shows blackletter working as liturgy in gold rather than as metal.

name: Darkest Dungeon logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Hand-cut flared gothic lettering in glowing red beside a torch emblem; a forum thread and a blog name Blambot's Dwarven Axe BB (commercial) for it, unverified, and the emblem is custom regardless.

name: Death's Door logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Chunky hand-cut serif where a door arch with the crow replaces a letter; appears custom (no font credit found), the lettering itself carries the story.

name: Inscryption logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Pixel-edged flared Roman capitals with an orange glow and a blood-ink drip; appears custom (no font credit found), pixel type made ominous.

name: Signalis logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: Ultra-light, widely tracked geometric capitals; appears custom (no font credit found), proof that a dark game can wear a quiet hairline logo.

name: Hades logo
licence: custom logo, reference only (image as served by its official Steam store page; not for reuse)
why: High-contrast Roman capitals with the A stretched into a bloody blade through the word; custom lettering (no font credit found), a logo that carries its premise in one gesture.
